attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition copies the statement and keeps the 'from what I can tell' qualifier and the timing. The qualifier says what his view rests on. It is not a probability hedge like may or likely, so the claim stays a scoreable observation.

contract.note: The contract tests his factual points: same entity, NFT/metaverse past, R1 on sale, $30M total funding. It checks 'disappearing' only loosely, as GAMA being shelved. That is an ordinary reading, not stretched either way.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous TechCrunch report calling Rabbit a rebranding of Cyber Manufacture Co. Backs 'same entity'.
Protos, published before the post. It says Cyber Manufacture was GAMA's parent and rebranded to Rabbit, that GAMA used NFTs, and that GAMA was put on hold.
Rabbit's own release, a company disclosure, putting total funding at $30M in Dec 2023. That matches the company-reported basis the contract asks for.
Engadget: R1 pre-orders from January 2024, batches sold out, first shipments from March 31. Rabbit was selling the device before May 2024.
Rabbit says GAMA was completed and then open-sourced. That still means the company stopped working on it, so it does not contradict 'shelved'. It also admits both projects came from the same company.

reviews.rationale: Independent press shows Rabbit is the renamed Cyber Manufacture, GAMA's NFT/metaverse company. Rabbit was selling the R1 by spring 2024 and reported $30M in total funding. GAMA was put on hold months before the R1 launched. Rabbit's 'completed and open-sourced' account is consistent with the project going dormant. Every element of the support condition is met.

Under the contract's fair reading, where GAMA's company is now Rabbit, 'is' holds. Rabbit's claim that Lyu left GAMA is about a project, not a separate company.

contract.note: Mission change means the rename plus a shift to AI within about a year. Abandoned means shelved or no longer developed. $6m is the GAMA raise. These are ordinary readings.

evidence.note: TechCrunch, Oct 2023: Cyber Manufacture rebranded as Rabbit and is now building an AI interface. That is the mission change, about seven months before the post.
Rabbit's spokesperson, via Coinspeaker, says the company rebranded and shifted its focus to AI. That is a company statement. The event date given is the rebrand.
Protos, before the post: a former GAMA engineer says GAMA was put on hold when priorities shifted to Rabbit.

Coinspeaker relays Findeisen's claim that the company raised $6M for an NFT project, and Rabbit's reported reply does not dispute it. This is weak support: a third party's claim, with the 2021-11 date taken from elsewhere.
Rabbit says GAMA was completed and then open-sourced. That still means the company stopped developing it, so it does not show GAMA as an active mission.

reviews.rationale: Press and Rabbit both confirm the rename and the shift to AI in October 2023, and GAMA was put on hold. Rabbit's 'completed and open-sourced' still means GAMA stopped being developed, which meets the hedged 'appears abandoned'. The $6M figure is reported in the press and not disputed by Rabbit, though it is the weakest link. Nothing shows GAMA stayed an active mission.
